# Styling

A guide to styling Base UI components with your preferred styling engine.

[View as Markdown](/react/handbook/styling.md)

Base UI components are unstyled, don’t bundle CSS, and are compatible with Tailwind, CSS Modules, CSS-in-JS, or any other styling solution you prefer. You retain total control of your styling layer.

## [Style hooks](#style-hooks)

### [CSS classes](#css-classes)

Components that render an HTML element accept a `className` prop to style the element with CSS classes.

switch.tsx

```tsx
<Switch.Thumb className="SwitchThumb" />
```

The prop can also be passed a function that takes the component’s state as an argument.

switch.tsx

```tsx
<Switch.Thumb className={(state) => (state.checked ? 'checked' : 'unchecked')} />
```

### [Data attributes](#data-attributes)

Components provide data attributes designed for styling their states. For example, [Switch](/react/components/switch) can be styled using its `[data-checked]` and `[data-unchecked]` attributes, among others.

switch.css

```css
.SwitchThumb[data-checked] {
  background-color: green;
}
```

### [CSS variables](#css-variables)

Components expose CSS variables to aid in styling, often containing dynamic numeric values to be used in sizing or transform calculations. For example, [Popover](/react/components/popover) exposes CSS variables on its `Popup` component like `--available-height` and `--anchor-width`.

popover.css

```css
.Popup {
  max-height: var(--available-height);
}
```

Check out each component’s API reference for a complete list of available data attributes and CSS variables.

### [Style prop](#style-prop)

Components that render an HTML element accept a `style` prop to style the element with a CSS object.

switch.tsx

```tsx
<Switch.Thumb style={{ height: '100px' }} />
```

The prop also accepts a function that takes the component’s state as an argument.

switch.tsx

```tsx
<Switch.Thumb style={(state) => ({ color: state.checked ? 'red' : 'blue' })} />
```

## [CSS Modules](#css-modules)

Apply custom CSS classes to each part via the `className` prop. Then style those classes in a CSS Modules file.

menu.tsx

```tsx
import { Menu } from '@base-ui/react/menu';
import styles from './menu.module.css';

export default function ExampleMenu() {
  return (
    <Menu.Root>
      <Menu.Trigger className={styles.Button}>Song</Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Portal>
        <Menu.Positioner className={styles.Positioner} sideOffset={8}>
          <Menu.Popup className={styles.Popup}>
            <Menu.Item className={styles.Item}>Add to Library</Menu.Item>
            <Menu.Item className={styles.Item}>Add to Playlist</Menu.Item>
          </Menu.Popup>
        </Menu.Positioner>
      </Menu.Portal>
    </Menu.Root>
  );
}
```

## [CSS-in-JS](#css-in-js)

Wrap each component part and apply styles, then assemble your styled components.

menu.tsx

```tsx
import { Menu } from '@base-ui/react/menu';
import styled from '@emotion/styled';

const StyledMenuTrigger = styled(Menu.Trigger)`
  // Button styles
`;

const StyledMenuPositioner = styled(Menu.Positioner)`
  // Positioner styles
`;

const StyledMenuPopup = styled(Menu.Popup)`
  // Popup styles
`;

const StyledMenuItem = styled(Menu.Item)`
  // Menu item styles
`;

const MenuExample = () => (
  <Menu.Root>
    <StyledMenuTrigger>Song</StyledMenuTrigger>
    <Menu.Portal>
      <StyledMenuPositioner>
        <StyledMenuPopup>
          <StyledMenuItem>Add to Library</StyledMenuItem>
          <StyledMenuItem>Add to Playlist</StyledMenuItem>
        </StyledMenuPopup>
      </StyledMenuPositioner>
    </Menu.Portal>
  </Menu.Root>
);

export default MenuExample;
```

# Contributing

Copy page

Learn how to contribute to Kumo, from setup and workflows to PR and release guidelines. Everything you need for setup, development, quality checks, and PR process is documented here.

Before You Start1\. Get Set Up Once Repository Access and Branching2\. Pick the Right Contribution Type3\. Start the Dev Loop4\. Implement the Change5\. Run Validation Before PR6\. Handle Changesets Correctly7\. Open and Maintain the PRPR Previews and TestsRelease Process (How Your Change Ships)Practical GuidelinesRelated Docs

## [Before You Start](#before-you-start)

For non-trivial changes, start with alignment before coding:

-   Comment on an existing issue or open one first.
-   Confirm scope, API direction, and migration impact.
-   For small fixes/docs tweaks, you can go straight to a PR.

---

## [1\. Get Set Up Once](#1-get-set-up-once)

From repo root:

```
pnpm install
pnpm build
```

Requirements:

-   Node `^24.12.0`
-   pnpm `>=10.26.0`

Recommended local setup:

-   Use a Node version manager (`nvm`, `fnm`, etc.).
-   Use VS Code and select the workspace TypeScript version.
-   If dependencies changed after rebase, run `pnpm install` again.

### [Repository Access and Branching](#repository-access-and-branching)

Internal contributors normally clone and push directly to `cloudflare/kumo`:

```
git clone https://github.com/cloudflare/kumo.git
git switch -c <branch-name>
git push -u origin <branch-name>
```

If you do not have write access, contact your manager or Kumo maintainers.

---

## [2\. Pick the Right Contribution Type](#2-pick-the-right-contribution-type)

Use this to decide where your change belongs:

-   **Component**: reusable UI primitive in `packages/kumo/src/components/`
-   **Block**: installable composition pattern in `packages/kumo/src/blocks/`
-   **Docs only**: docs/demo/navigation updates in `packages/kumo-docs-astro/`

When adding a new **component**, scaffold it (do not create files manually):

```
pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo new:component
```

---

## [3\. Start the Dev Loop](#3-start-the-dev-loop)

Run these in separate terminals:

```
# Terminal 1: watch Kumo package output
pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo dev

# Terminal 2: docs site
pnpm dev
```

This gives you a fast loop while verifying your change in the actual docs environment.

---

## [4\. Implement the Change](#4-implement-the-change)

Typical internal change flow:

1.  Build the feature in `packages/kumo/src/...`.
2.  Add or update demos in `packages/kumo-docs-astro/src/components/demos/`.
3.  Add/update tests in `packages/kumo`.
4.  Add or update docs pages in `packages/kumo-docs-astro/src/pages/`.

If your demos should appear in registry metadata, keep demo naming exact:

-   File: `{Component}Demo.tsx`
-   Export names must end with `Demo`

Implementation expectations:

-   Preserve accessibility semantics and keyboard behavior.
-   Keep APIs focused and avoid one-off abstractions.
-   Follow existing Kumo patterns for variants, props, and structure.

---

## [5\. Run Validation Before PR](#5-run-validation-before-pr)

Run these from repo root before opening or updating your PR:

```
pnpm lint
pnpm typecheck
pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo test
```

If you changed exports/build behavior, also run:

```
pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo build
```

Optional (when relevant):

```
pnpm format
pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo test:run
```

Windsurf and hooks catch additional issues, but you should still run checks locally before requesting review.

---

## [6\. Handle Changesets Correctly](#6-handle-changesets-correctly)

If your change touches `packages/kumo/` and should ship, add a changeset:

```
pnpm changeset
```

Changeset guidance:

-   Use `patch` for bug fixes and low-risk improvements.
-   Use `minor` for new backward-compatible features.
-   Use `major` only for breaking changes.
-   Keep the summary focused on user-visible impact.

If your change is docs-only or non-releasable package work, a changeset is usually not required.

---

## [7\. Open and Maintain the PR](#7-open-and-maintain-the-pr)

-   Branch from `main` and push to `origin`.
-   Use PR title format: `[package] short description` (example: `[kumo] add meter warning variant`).
-   Fill in the PR template with testing details and impact.
-   After review starts, prefer follow-up commits over force-pushing rewritten history.

Git hygiene expectations:

-   Keep commit history readable before first review.
-   After reviews begin, avoid rewriting already-reviewed commits.
-   Add follow-up commits for feedback (`fixup` commits are fine).

PR review is required before merge.

---

## [PR Previews and Tests](#pr-previews-and-tests)

-   PRs publish prerelease artifacts via `pkg.pr.new` links in CI comments.
-   Every PR should include tests for behavior changes.
-   Most Kumo tests are Vitest-based and live under `packages/kumo`.

---

## [Release Process (How Your Change Ships)](#release-process-how-your-change-ships)

-   Releases are managed through Changesets.
-   Merged changesets on `main` feed the automated versioning/publish flow.
-   If you need an urgent out-of-cadence release, contact maintainers.

---

## [Practical Guidelines](#practical-guidelines)

-   Use semantic Kumo tokens and avoid raw Tailwind color classes.
-   Compose class names with `cn(...)`.
-   Prefer extending existing patterns over introducing one-off API designs.
-   Include tests for behavior changes, not just rendering snapshots.

Common pitfalls to avoid:

-   Do not scaffold components manually; use `new:component`.
-   Do not rely on raw Tailwind color classes (`bg-blue-500`, etc.).
-   Do not skip changesets for releasable `packages/kumo` changes.

---

## [Related Docs](#related-docs)

Follow the [changeset guide](https://github.com/cloudflare/kumo/blob/main/.changeset/README.md) to document releasable library changes and see the [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/cloudflare/kumo/blob/main/packages/kumo/AGENTS.md) for conventions and patterns.

I want to create a README template so amazing that it'll be the last one you ever need -- I think this is it.\n\nHere's why:\n* Your time should be focused on creating something amazing. A project that solves a problem and helps others\n* You shouldn't be doing the same tasks over and over like creating a README from scratch\n* You should implement DRY principles to the rest of your life :smile:\n\nOf course, no one template will serve all projects since your needs may be different. # Component Library (`@cloudflare/kumo`)

React component library: Base UI + Tailwind v4 + Vite library mode. ESM-only, tree-shakeable per-component exports.

**Parent:** See [root AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) for monorepo context.

## STRUCTURE

```
kumo/
├── src/
│   ├── components/          # 39 UI components → see src/components/AGENTS.md
│   ├── blocks/              # Installable blocks (NOT library exports; via CLI `kumo add`)
│   ├── primitives/          # AUTO-GENERATED Base UI re-exports (40 files)
│   ├── catalog/             # JSON-UI rendering runtime (DynamicValue, visibility conditions)
│   ├── code/                # Shiki-based code highlighting (lazy-loaded, 16 bundled languages)
│   ├── command-line/        # CLI: ls, doc, add, blocks, init, migrate
│   ├── styles/              # CSS: kumo-binding.css + theme files (AUTO-GENERATED)
│   ├── utils/               # cn(), safeRandomId, LinkProvider
│   ├── registry/            # Type-only exports for registry metadata
│   └── index.ts             # Main barrel export (PLOP_INJECT_EXPORT marker)
├── ai/                      # AUTO-GENERATED: component-registry.{json,md}, schemas.ts
├── scripts/
│   ├── component-registry/  # Registry codegen (13 sub-modules, 930+ lines orchestrator)
│   ├── theme-generator/     # Theme CSS codegen from config.ts
│   ├── generate-primitives.ts
│   └── css-build.ts         # Post-Vite CSS processing
├── lint/                    # 5 custom oxlint rules (superset of root lint/)
├── tests/imports/           # Structural validation: export paths, package.json, build entries
├── vite.config.ts           # Library mode, dynamic primitive discovery, PLOP marker
└── vitest.config.ts         # happy-dom, v8 coverage, path aliases
```

## WHERE TO LOOK

| Task                     | Location                                        | Notes                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Component implementation | `src/components/{name}/{name}.tsx`              | Always check registry first                                                |
| Component API reference  | `ai/component-registry.json`                    | Source of truth for props/variants                                         |
| Variant definitions      | `KUMO_{NAME}_VARIANTS` export in component file | Machine-readable + lint-enforced                                           |
| CLI commands             | `src/command-line/commands/`                    | `ls`, `doc`, `add`, `blocks`, `init`, `migrate`                            |
| Catalog runtime          | `src/catalog/`                                  | JSON pointer resolution, visibility conditions                             |
| Code highlighting        | `src/code/`                                     | ShikiProvider, lazy-loaded highlighter, 16 bundled languages               |
| Blocks source            | `src/blocks/{name}/`                            | Installed to consumers via CLI, not exported                               |
| Scaffold new component   | `plopfile.js`                                   | Injects into index.ts, vite.config.ts, package.json                        |
| Token definitions        | `scripts/theme-generator/config.ts`             | Source of truth; generates theme CSS                                       |
| Registry codegen         | `scripts/component-registry/index.ts`           | 13 sub-modules; pipeline: discovery → cache → type extraction → enrichment |

## CONVENTIONS

### Build System

- **Three-step build**: `vp build` (Vite+/Rolldown) → `css-build.ts` (copies CSS + `@tailwindcss/cli`) → `build-cli.ts` (esbuild)
- **Bundled deps**: `@base-ui/react`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge` are bundled (not external)
- **External peers**: `react`, `react-dom`, `@phosphor-icons/react` only
- **`"use client"` banner**: Injected on ALL output chunks for RSC compatibility
- **`sideEffects: ["*.css"]`**: Only CSS is side-effectful; enables aggressive tree-shaking
- **Manual chunks**: `vendor-styling`, `vendor-floating-ui`, `vendor-base-ui`, `vendor-utils`

### Component File Pattern

See `src/components/AGENTS.md` for detailed component conventions.

### Registry Codegen Pipeline

```
kumo-docs-astro demos → dist/demo-metadata.json  (cross-package dependency!)
                              ↓
ts-json-schema-generator → TypeScript type extraction
                              ↓
Enrichment: variants + examples + sub-components + styling metadata
                              ↓
Output: ai/component-registry.{json,md} + ai/schemas.ts
```

- **Cache**: Hash-based at `.cache/component-registry-cache.json`. Bypass: `--no-cache`
- **Parallel**: Processes components in batches of 8
- **Fallback**: If type extraction fails, falls back to variants-only props (silent)
- **Metadata overrides**: `scripts/component-registry/metadata.ts` has manual `ADDITIONAL_COMPONENT_PROPS`, `PROP_TYPE_OVERRIDES`

### Testing

- **Vitest** with `happy-dom`, globals enabled
- **Path aliases**: `@/` → `src/`, `@cloudflare/kumo` → `src/index.ts`
- **Structural tests** in `tests/imports/`: validate all export paths resolve, package.json matches vite entries
- **Component tests**: ~14 components have unit tests (`*.test.tsx`), plus 2 browser tests (`*.browser.test.tsx`). Coverage is growing but not comprehensive across all 39 components
- **`describe.skipIf(!isBuilt)`**: Export validation tests skip gracefully when `dist/` missing

## ANTI-PATTERNS

| Pattern                                              | Why                                    | Instead                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Editing `src/primitives/`                            | Auto-generated from Base UI            | Run `pnpm codegen:primitives`        |
| Editing `ai/schemas.ts` or `ai/component-registry.*` | Auto-generated at build time           | Edit source files, CI generates them |
| Creating component files manually                    | Misses index/vite/package.json updates | `pnpm new:component`                 |
| `as any` in component code                           | 3 existing instances; don't add more   | Model types correctly                |
| Dynamic Tailwind class construction                  | JIT can't detect `leading-[${val}]`    | Use static class strings             |

## DEPRECATED COMPONENTS/PROPS

### Components

| Component         | Replacement                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `DateRangePicker` | Use `DatePicker` with `mode="range"` |

### Props (lint-enforced via `no-deprecated-props`)

| Component           | Prop                                | Replacement                                              |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Select`            | `hideLabel`                         | Use `aria-label` instead of `label` + `hideLabel={true}` |
| `DropdownMenu.Item` | `href`                              | Use `DropdownMenu.LinkItem` for navigation               |
| `Checkbox`          | `onChange`, `onIndeterminateChange` | Use `onCheckedChange`                                    |
| `Banner`            | `text`, `children`                  | Use `title` and `description` props                      |
| `TimeseriesChart`   | `formatValue`                       | Use `tooltipValueFormat`                                 |
| `Code`              | `CodeLanguage` type                 | Use `CodeLang` type                                      |

## NOTES

- **Compound components**: CommandPalette (14 sub-components), Dialog, Select use two-level contexts
- **13 components use createContext**: SwitchGroup, PaginationContext, RadioGroup, FlowNodeAnchor, Diagram, Descendants, InputGroup, DialogRole, ComboboxSize, Grid, CheckboxGroup, CommandPalette (2)
- **DateRangePicker**: Contains 150 lines of duplicated ternary logic (refactoring target)
- **Catalog `initCatalog`**: Appears to have race condition with async schema loading
- **CLI path inconsistency**: `ls`/`doc` read from `catalog/`, `blocks` from `ai/` directory
- **`PLOP_INJECT_EXPORT`** in `src/index.ts` and `PLOP_INJECT_COMPONENT_ENTRY` in `vite.config.ts` are scaffolding markers
- **5th lint rule** (`no-deprecated-props`): Only in `packages/kumo/lint/`, reads deprecation data from registry
- **LinkProvider**: Framework-agnostic link abstraction; wrap app with custom Link component (e.g., Next.js)

## [Canary releases](#canary-releases)

A canary release is published for every master commit and pull request. Install one by using the corresponding pkg.pr.new URL:

Terminal

```shell
# Install by master commit hash
npm i https://pkg.pr.new/@base-ui/react@ad745f1

# Install by PR number
npm i https://pkg.pr.new/@base-ui/react@3713
```

Your `package.json` will then reference the pkg.pr.new URL:

package.json

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@base-ui/react": "https://pkg.pr.new/@base-ui/react@..."
  }
}
```

Canary releases may contain breaking changes. Check the associated pull requests on GitHub for details.

# About Base UI

An open-source React component library for building accessible user interfaces.

[View as Markdown](/react/overview/about.md)

From the creators of Radix, Material UI, and Floating UI, Base UI is an unstyled React component library for building accessible user interfaces. Our focus is on accessibility, performance, and developer experience. Our goal is to provide a complete set of open-source UI components, with a delightful developer experience, in a sustainable way.

## [Features](#features)

### [Headless](#headless)

Base UI components are unstyled, don’t bundle CSS, and don’t prescribe a styling solution. You retain complete control over your application’s CSS layer. Base UI is compatible with Tailwind, CSS Modules, plain CSS, CSS-in-JS, or any other styling engine you prefer.

### [Accessible](#accessible)

Poor accessibility can make your application difficult to navigate for all users, not just for users with disabilities. Accessibility is our primary focus. Base UI components adhere to [WAI-ARIA design patterns](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/) and are tested on a wide range of platforms, devices, browsers, screen readers, and other environments.

### [Composable](#composable)

Component APIs are fully open, so you have direct access to each node, you can easily add or remove parts, and you can wrap them however you prefer.

## [Browser support](#browser-support)

Base UI supports all modern browsers that implement features marked as [Baseline Widely Available](https://web.dev/baseline) at the time of the last major version release. This means the features we use have been supported across major browsers for at least 30 months, ensuring broad compatibility and stability.

For the full list of supported browsers, refer to our [.browserslistrc](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/master/.browserslistrc).

## [React versions](#react-versions)

Base UI supports React 17 and newer versions.

## [Bundler support](#bundler-support)

Base UI works with maintained versions of all popular bundlers, including Vite, webpack, Turbopack and Parcel.

Your wrapper component receives `href` and is responsible for bridging to your router’s API. This lets engineers use `` everywhere without thinking about routing internals. ``` import { forwardRef } from "react"; import { LinkProvider } from "@cloudflare/kumo"; import { Link as RouterLink } from "react-router-dom"; // Your app's wrapper maps href to the router's navigation prop // and handles external URLs with a plain const AppLink = forwardRef(({ href, to, ...rest }, ref) => { const destination = href ?? to; const isExternal = destination?.startsWith("http") && new URL(destination).origin !== window.location.origin; if (isExternal) { return ; } return ; }); // Wrap your app once export function App() { return ( {/* All calls go through AppLink */} ); } ``` ### [Composition with render prop](#composition-with-render-prop) For exceptional cases where you need direct control over the rendered element, use the `render` prop. This bypasses the `LinkProvider` entirely — all other props (`href`, `target`, `className`, etc.) are merged onto the provided element automatically. ``` import { Link } from "@cloudflare/kumo"; import { Link as RouterLink } from "react-router-dom"; export default function Example() { return ( <> {/* Force a specific router link (bypasses LinkProvider) */} } variant="inline"> Dashboard {/* Force a plain anchor (bypasses LinkProvider) */} } href="https://example.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"> External Site ); } ``` ## [Examples](#examples) ### [Inline in Paragraph](#inline-in-paragraph) Links flow naturally within paragraph text with proper underline offset. Links maintain proper underline offset for readability. ``` import { Link } from "@cloudflare/kumo"; export function LinkInParagraphDemo() { return (

Prop Type Default Description variant “inline” | “current” | “plain" "inline” Visual style variant render ReactElement \- Element to render with Link props merged onto it href string \- Link destination URL. Use this for all links — both internal and external. Configure a `LinkProvider` to bridge `href` to your router. to string \- **Deprecated.** Use `href` instead. This prop will be removed in a future major version. className string \- Additional CSS classes children ReactNode \- Link content ### [Variants](#variants) Variant Description Use Case inline Primary color with underline Default for inline text links current Inherits parent text color with underline Links within colored contexts (alerts, errors) plain Primary color without underline Navigation links, menus, footers ### [Link.ExternalIcon](#linkexternalicon) SVG icon component to indicate external links. Accepts all SVG element attributes. ``` External Site ``` ## [Design Guidelines](#design-guidelines) ### [When to Use Each Variant](#when-to-use-each-variant) - **inline**: Default choice for links within body text - **current**: Links inside alerts, banners, or other colored containers - **plain**: Navigation menus, footers, or where underlines are distracting ### [External Link Indicators](#external-link-indicators) - Always use `Link.ExternalIcon` for links that open in new tabs - Set `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` for security - The icon provides a visual cue that users will leave the current site ### [Framework Integration](#framework-integration) - Configure a `LinkProvider` at your app root to integrate with your client-side router - Your wrapper receives `href` and maps it to your router’s navigation prop (e.g. React Router’s `to`) - The wrapper should handle external URLs by rendering a plain `<a>` instead of routing them - Use the `render` prop as an escape hatch for exceptional cases that need direct control over the rendered element - The `to` prop is deprecated — use `href` for all link destinations ### [Accessibility](#accessibility) - Use these classes in your Tailwind CSS instead of raw color values. UsageModeThemes Available Themes Theme Generator Creating a New ThemeSemantic Tokens Surface Hierarchy Brand Semantic Status Colors Text Colors Borders & RingsToken Reference ## [Usage](#usage) Always use semantic tokens instead of raw Tailwind colors. This ensures your UI automatically adapts to light and dark mode, and that your components remain consistent across themes. #### [Correct](#correct) ```
``` #### [Incorrect](#incorrect) ``` { /* Never use raw Tailwind colors */ }
; ``` > Lint rules enforce this: The `no-primitive-colors` rule will flag any raw Tailwind colors like `bg-blue-500`. ## [Mode](#mode) Set `data-mode` on a parent element to control light/dark mode. Never use Tailwind’s `dark:` variant — semantic tokens handle dark mode automatically via CSS `light-dark()`. ``` // Set mode on html or body // Light mode // Dark mode // Components automatically adapt - no dark: variants needed
``` ## [Themes](#themes) Themes override semantic token values while preserving the same token names. Set `data-theme` on a parent element to apply a theme. ### [Available Themes](#available-themes) - `kumo` — Default theme (no attribute needed) - `fedramp` — Government compliance styling ``` // Apply a theme to a section or the whole app
{/* All Kumo components inside use fedramp token overrides */}
// Themes work with both light and dark mode ``` ### [Theme Generator](#theme-generator) Themes are defined in a centralized config and generated as CSS files. The theme generator ensures consistency across all themes. ``` # List all tokens and their theme overrides pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo codegen:themes --list # Generate theme CSS files pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo codegen:themes # Preview changes without writing files pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo codegen:themes --dry-run ``` Theme config: `packages/kumo/scripts/theme-generator/config.ts` ### [Creating a New Theme](#creating-a-new-theme) Add theme overrides in the config file. Only override tokens that need to change — all other tokens inherit from the base kumo theme. ``` // In scripts/theme-generator/config.ts export const THEME_CONFIG: ThemeConfig = { color: { "kumo-base": { newName: "", theme: { kumo: { light: "var(--color-white, #fff)", dark: "var(--color-black, #000)", }, // Add your theme override myTheme: { light: "#f0f4f8", dark: "#1a1f2e", }, }, }, // ... other tokens }, }; // Add to available themes export const AVAILABLE_THEMES = ["kumo", "fedramp", "myTheme"] as const; ``` Then run `pnpm codegen:themes` to generate the CSS. ## [Semantic Tokens](#semantic-tokens) We use semantic tokens to group colors by purpose. Use the token that matches the role of the element, not the color you want to achieve. Semantic tokens are named by **role**, not by hue. A token like `bg-kumo-danger` communicates intent — it doesn’t imply a specific shade of red, and its exact value can change per theme or color mode without touching your component code. ### [Surface Hierarchy](#surface-hierarchy) Surfaces establish depth and layering in the UI. Use them in order from the outermost background inward. Token Purpose `bg-kumo-canvas` The outermost page background — sits behind everything `bg-kumo-base` Default component background `bg-kumo-elevated` Slightly elevated surface, e.g. `LayerCard.Secondary` `bg-kumo-recessed` Recessed surface with a subtly darker fill, e.g. segmented `Tabs` background `bg-kumo-tint` Subtle tinted background for tables or hover states `bg-kumo-contrast` High-contrast, inverted background ### [Brand](#brand) Token Purpose `bg-kumo-brand` Primary brand background `bg-kumo-brand-hover` Hover state for brand backgrounds ### [Semantic Status Colors](#semantic-status-colors) Each status color comes in two variants: a solid color for icons and indicators, and a `-tint` variant for background fills behind content (i.e. `Badge` or `Banner`). Token Purpose `bg-kumo-info` Info indicator `bg-kumo-success` Success indicator `bg-kumo-warning` Warning indicator `bg-kumo-danger` Error/destructive indicator Use the solid token `bg-kumo-*` for status dots, `fill-kumo-*` for icons, and `border-kumo-*`, `ring-kumo-*` for borders and rings. Banners and badges use the `-tint` variant with varying opacity values. Something went wrong. ``` import { WarningIcon } from "@phosphor-icons/react"; export function StatusBannerDemo() { return (

## [Installation](#installation)

```
npx skills add cloudflare/kumo@kumo-design
```

## [Rules](#rules)

### 1.Use 14px for content text

All content text—body, buttons, data, other interactables—must be 14px in size. 16px and above are restricted to headings and subheadings.

Recommended example

### 2.Always sentence case headings

Never capitalize or uppercase headings. Product names must be title-cased.

Recommended example

### 3.Never change the font's tracking

Do not use the `tracking-*` classes to change the spacing between characters.

Recommended example

Example to avoid

### 4.Never use `font-bold`

Use `font-semibold` for headings and `font-medium` for bold inline text.

Recommended example

### 5.Put related text closer together

Related text should have smaller spacing around it than the content it belongs to.

### 6.Optically align spacing around text

Spacing around text should take into account its line height. Typically this means vertical spacing should be slightly smaller than horizontal.

### 7.Never transition colors for hover states

Color changes on hover must be immediate. Transitions on fast interactions make the UI feel sluggish.

Recommended example

### 8.Never use borders with drop shadows

Use `ring ring-kumo-line` to create a transparent border that maintains sharp edges.

### 9.Use concentric border radii

When borders or rings are 8px or less apart, their corner radii must be mathematically concentric: outer radius = inner radius + padding.

### 10.Align icons with the first line of text

Inline icons must be optically the same size as and be center-aligned with text. Use `h-lh flex items-center` for multi-line alignment.

Monospaced text should have a slightly smaller font size (~0.9em) when mixed with regular text.

Collapsible content must maintain its content size while closing to avoid its content shifting during animations.

### 15.Never conditionally render dialogs

Conditionally rendering dialogs disables their open/close animation. Use the `open` prop to determine if a dialog should be visible or not.

Recommended example

```
<Dialog.Root open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <Dialog>
    <Dialog.Title>Edit Worker</Dialog.Title>
    <Dialog.Description>Update this Worker's settings.</Dialog.Description>
  </Dialog>
</Dialog.Root>
```

Example to avoid

```
{open && (
  <Dialog.Root open>
    <Dialog>
      <Dialog.Title>Edit Worker</Dialog.Title>
    </Dialog>
  </Dialog.Root>
)}
```

## [Overview](#overview)

The component registry is a machine-readable JSON file that describes all Kumo components, their props, variants, examples, and semantic tokens. It’s designed for AI agents, code generators, and other tooling.

[View JSON API](/api/component-registry)

## [Accessing the Registry](#accessing-the-registry)

### [Via CLI](#via-cli)

```
# List all components
npx @cloudflare/kumo ls

# Get docs for a specific component
npx @cloudflare/kumo doc Button
```

### [Via HTTP API](#via-http-api)

```
# JSON endpoint
curl https://kumo-ui.com/api/component-registry
```

### [Via jq (Local)](#via-jq-local)

```
# Get Button props
jq '.components.Button.props' packages/kumo/ai/component-registry.json

# List components by category
jq '.search.byCategory' packages/kumo/ai/component-registry.json
```

The registry includes: component props with types and defaults, variant options with descriptions, real code examples from stories, semantic color tokens used, and sub-components for compound patterns.

This is the documentation for the `@base-ui/react` package.
It contains a collection of components and utilities for building user interfaces in React.
The library is designed to be composable and styling agnostic.
The Tailwind CSS examples are written for Tailwind CSS v4. If `package.json` uses Tailwind CSS v3, automatically convert unsupported styles to v3-compatible equivalents.

This includes animating its position, size, and content. #### Position and Size To animate the popover’s position, apply CSS transitions to the `left`, `right`, `top`, and `bottom` properties of the **Positioner** part. To animate its size, transition the `width` and `height` of the **Popup** part. #### Content The popover also supports content transitions. This is useful when different triggers display different content within the same popover. To enable content animations, wrap the content in the `` part. This part provides features to create direction-aware animations. It renders a `div` with a `data-activation-direction` attribute that indicates the new trigger’s position relative to the previous one. The value is a space-separated set of up to two tokens (one per axis) — `left` or `right` for the horizontal axis and `up` or `down` for the vertical axis (for example, `right down`). Match a single token with the `~=` attribute selector, such as `[data-activation-direction~='right']`. Inside the ``, the content is further wrapped in `div`s with data attributes to help with styling: - `data-current`: The currently visible content when no transitions are present or the incoming content. - `data-previous`: The outgoing content during a transition. You can use these attributes to style the enter and exit animations. v4.12.34

\n

Security fixes

\n

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

\n

memo() retains SSR output across requests, leading to cross-user data disclosure

\n

Affects: hono/jsx (server-side rendering). Fixes memo() reusing a retained render result across requests when props compare equal, where a component reading request-scoped values from ambient context — useContext(), useRequestContext(), or getContext() — could serve HTML rendered for another user's request, disclosing account data or request-scoped secrets such as CSRF tokens. GHSA-f23p-vx2j-j53r

\n

ReDoS in CORS middleware via Access-Control-Request-Headers

\n

Affects: hono/cors. Fixes a whitespace-tolerant regular expression with quadratic backtracking used to parse the Access-Control-Request-Headers preflight header when allowHeaders is not configured (the default), where a single preflight request carrying a long whitespace run could consume seconds of CPU and stall request processing. GHSA-8j4g-w8fx-2239

\n

Algorithmic complexity DoS in Language Middleware

\n

Affects: hono/language. Fixes quadratic string processing in language-tag normalization, where a crafted language tag with a large number of hyphen-separated subtags — supplied via a query parameter, cookie, or Accept-Language header — could cause excessive CPU consumption and block the event loop. GHSA-54fx-42gc-7vw4

\n

Proxy Helper does not remove response headers listed in the Connection header

\n

Affects: hono/proxy. Fixes proxy() forwarding response headers that the origin's Connection header designates as connection-scoped, where headers intended only for the immediate peer — per RFC 9110 Section 7.6.1 — could be exposed to clients, disclosing connection-scoped or internal metadata. GHSA-79qm-7rj5-m7r9

\n
\n

Users who use hono/jsx for server-side rendering, hono/cors, hono/language, or hono/proxy are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

      "body": "## Problem\n\n`Sidebar.useIsMobile` reads `window.matchMedia` inside a `useState` initializer:\n\n```ts\nconst [isMobile, setIsMobile] = useState(() => {\n  if (typeof window === \"undefined\") return false;\n  return window.matchMedia(`(max-width: ${breakpoint - 1}px)`).matches;\n});\n```\n\nDuring SSR `window` is undefined, so `isMobile` is `false` (desktop) and the server renders the desktop `<aside>`. On a mobile viewport the client's first hydration render evaluates `matchMedia` → `true`, producing the **mobile overlay DOM** (a structurally different tree: backdrop + `<nav data-mobile>`). The SSR HTML and the client hydration render don't match → React logs a hard hydration mismatch error and re-renders client-side, discarding the SSR output.\n\nThis affects any SSR framework (e.g. Next.js) mounting `Sidebar` on a mobile viewport. Confirmed still present on `main` and in the latest published versions (2.9.2 / 2.10.0).\n\n## Fix\n\nSwitch `useIsMobile` to `useSyncExternalStore` with a desktop `getServerSnapshot`:\n\n- **Hydration is SSR-safe**: React renders with `getServerSnapshot` (`false`) during hydration, matching the SSR HTML, then switches to the real viewport once subscribed to `matchMedia`.\n- **No re-subscribe churn**: `subscribe`/`getSnapshot` are memoized on the query, so the `matchMedia` listener only re-binds when the `breakpoint` changes — same behavior as the previous `useEffect([breakpoint])`.\n\n```ts\nfunction useIsMobile(breakpoint: number = MOBILE_BREAKPOINT) {\n  const query = `(max-width: ${breakpoint - 1}px)`;\n\n  const subscribe = useCallback((callback: () => void) => {\n    const mql = window.matchMedia(query);\n    mql.addEventListener(\"change\", callback);\n    return () => mql.removeEventListener(\"change\", callback);\n  }, [query]);\n\n  const getSnapshot = useCallback(\n    () => window.matchMedia(query).matches,\n    [query],\n  );\n\n  const getServerSnapshot = useCallback(() => false, []);\n\n  return useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getServerSnapshot);\n}\n```\n\n## Tests\n\nAdded 4 unit tests in `sidebar.test.tsx` covering the SSR/hydration contract:\n\n- SSR renders the desktop `<aside>` regardless of the viewport (fails with the previous implementation).\n- `hydrateRoot` over the SSR output produces no hydration mismatch on a mobile viewport.\n- Client render on a mobile viewport yields the mobile overlay.\n- Client render on a desktop viewport yields the desktop `<aside>`.\n\n- Reviews\n  - [ ] bonk has reviewed the change\n  - [x] automated review not possible because: external contribution\n- Tests\n  - [x] Tests included/updated",

      "body": "## Summary\r\n\r\nAdds an optional `autoResize` prop to `InputArea` and its `Textarea` alias. When enabled, the textarea grows vertically with its content.\r\n\r\n## Changes\r\n\r\n- Resize the textarea on initial render and value changes\r\n- Preserve `onChange`, `onValueChange`, and forwarded ref behavior\r\n- Hide the manual resize handle while automatic resizing is enabled\r\n- Add unit tests and a documentation example\r\n- Add a minor changeset for `@cloudflare/kumo`\r\n\r\n## Implementation note\r\n\r\n`field-sizing: content` is used as a progressive enhancement for the server-rendered, pre-hydration frame. `w-full` constrains its inline size so it only grows vertically. After hydration, the `scrollHeight` measurement applies the explicit height and enforces `minRows` and `maxRows`; browsers without `field-sizing` support use the same JavaScript path as a fallback.\r\n\r\n## Testing\r\n\r\n- `CI=true pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo exec vitest run --project=unit src/components/input/input.test.tsx`\r\n- `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo typecheck`\r\n- `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo lint`\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n<!--\r\nPlease don't delete the checkboxes <3\r\nThe following selections do not need to be completed if this PR only contains changes to .md files\r\n-->\r\n\r\n- Reviews\r\n  - [ ] bonk has reviewed the change\r\n  - [x] automated review not possible because: this focused component enhancement will receive normal PR review\r\n- Tests\r\n  - [x] Tests included/updated\r\n  - [ ] Automated tests not possible - manual testing has been completed as follows:\r\n  - [ ] Additional testing not necessary because:\r\n\r\n<!--\r\nHave you read our [Contributing guide](https://github.com/cloudflare/kumo/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)?\r\nIn particular, for non-trivial changes, please always engage on the issue or create a discussion or feature request issue first before writing your code.\r\n-->\r",

      "body": "Fixes two issues on the timeseries chart docs page:\n\n**Empty Table of Contents**\nAll section headings were `###` (h3) with no `##` (h2) parents. The `TableOfContents` component groups h3s under h2s and silently drops orphaned h3s, so the TOC rendered empty. Promoted all headings to h2.\n\n**Broken loading state demo**\nThe `LoadingChartDemo` uses `useIsDarkMode()` which reads from the DOM. During SSR, it defaults to light mode and renders the wave SVG with a dark stroke color. On client hydration in dark mode, React detects the attribute mismatch and refuses to patch it — resulting in an invisible wave (black stroke on dark background). Switched to `client:only=\"react\"` to skip SSR entirely.\n\n---\n\n- Reviews\n- [ ] bonk has reviewed the change\n- [x] automated review not possible because: docs-only change with no component logic\n- Tests\n- [x] Additional testing not necessary because: docs-only MDX heading level and hydration directive change, verified locally",

      "body": "## Summary\n\nThe docs site (`kumo-ui.com`) felt sluggish to navigate. It turns out the site is **already fully static** (`output: \"static\"`, no SSR adapter, `dist/` served as Cloudflare static assets) — the slowness wasn't server rendering. It came from:\n\n- Classic full-page reloads on every link click\n- **No prefetch** — each navigation was a cold fetch\n- Heavy React island hydration (**113 `client:load` + 331 `client:visible`**) re-booting on every page load\n\nThis PR makes navigation feel instant without changing the static output.\n\n## Changes\n\n- **Hover prefetch** (`astro.config.mjs`): `prefetch: { prefetchAll: true, defaultStrategy: \"hover\" }` — target pages are fetched the moment a link is hovered/focused.\n- **Soft navigation** via `<ClientRouter />` (`BaseLayout.astro`) — view-transition navigation instead of cold document reloads. (`MainLayout` already had an `astro:after-swap` scroll-restore handler written in anticipation of this; it was dead until now.)\n- **View-transition-safe scripts** (`BaseLayout.astro`):\n  - Theme init reapplies on `astro:before-swap`/`astro:after-swap`; keydown listener registered once behind a guard.\n  - Copy-button logic split so the click delegation registers once and `wrapCodeBlocks()` re-runs on `astro:page-load` (prevents lost buttons / stacked listeners).\n- **Persisted sidebar** (`MainLayout.astro` + `SidebarNav.tsx`): `transition:persist` keeps the heavy `SidebarNav` island mounted across navigations. Since a persisted island won't receive a fresh `currentPath` prop, it now tracks the live pathname via `astro:page-load` so the active-link highlight stays correct.\n\n## Notes\n\n- Docs-only change — no `@cloudflare/kumo` library changes, so no changeset.\n- Follow-up idea (separate PR): audit the 113 `client:load` islands and downgrade non-critical ones to `client:visible`/`client:idle` to cut initial JS.\n\n## Test in preview\n\nNavigate around the docs (sidebar links, component pages) — clicks should feel instant, theme toggle + copy buttons should still work across soft navigations, and the active sidebar link should track the current page.\n\n- Reviews\n- [ ] bonk has reviewed the change\n- [x] automated review not possible because: perceived-performance / navigation UX change best verified by a human in the preview link\n- Tests\n- [ ] Tests included/updated\n- [x] Additional testing not necessary because: docs-only navigation enhancement with no library/API changes; build passes (71 static pages) and behavior is verified interactively in the preview deploy\n",

      "body": "## Summary\n\nFixes React hydration mismatch error in TableOfContents component when `headings` prop is not provided (i.e., when scraping headings from the DOM).\n\n**The problem:**\n- Server: `scrapeHeadings()` returns `[]` because `document` is undefined\n- Client: `scrapeHeadings()` returns actual headings from the DOM\n- This mismatch causes React to throw a hydration error\n\n**The fix:**\nDefer DOM scraping until after the component has mounted by tracking `hasMounted` state. On initial render (both server and client), we return an empty array. After mount, we re-run the memo and scrape the actual headings.\n\n---\n\n- Reviews\n  - [x] automated review not possible because: simple hydration fix, no complex logic changes\n- Tests\n  - [x] Additional testing not necessary because: fix verified by absence of console hydration errors in dev",

      "body": "Bumps [astro](https://github.com/withastro/astro/tree/HEAD/packages/astro) from 5.18.1 to 6.1.10.\n<details>\n<summary>Release notes</summary>\n<p><em>Sourced from <a href=\"https://github.com/withastro/astro/releases\">astro's releases</a>.</em></p>\n<blockquote>\n<h2>astro@5.18.2</h2>\n<h3>Patch Changes</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"https://redirect.github.com/withastro/astro/pull/16813\">#16813</a> <a href=\"https://github.com/withastro/astro/commit/8f7d8c46ffc79b23200a98fcf6b72c53e19d71db\"><code>8f7d8c4</code></a> Thanks <a href=\"https://github.com/matthewp\"><code>@​matthewp</code></a>! - Populates styles in the SSR manifest for prerendered routes. Previously, prerendered routes had <code>styles: []</code> in the manifest, making it impossible for workers or middleware to discover which CSS files a prerendered page uses.</li>\n</ul>\n</blockquote>\n</details>\n<details>\n<summary>Changelog</summary>\n<p><em>Sourced from <a href=\"https://github.com/withastro/astro/blob/main/packages/astro/CHANGELOG.md\">astro's changelog</a>.</em></p>\n<blockquote>\n<h2>6.1.10</h2>\n<h3>Patch Changes</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>\n<p><a href=\"https://redirect.github.com/withastro/astro/pull/16479\">#16479</a> <a href=\"https://github.com/withastro/astro/commit/1058428df2d13878c6130787636dd1778273a934\"><code>1058428</code></a> Thanks <a href=\"https://github.com/matthewp\"><code>@​matthewp</code></a>! - Fixes a spurious <code>[WARN] [content] Content config not loaded</code> warning during <code>astro dev</code> for projects that don't use content collections</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><a href=\"https://redirect.github.com/withastro/astro/pull/16457\">#16457</a> <a href=\"https://github.com/withastro/astro/commit/3d82220a1549e699e34ed433f3846a919f4c02bd\"><code>3d82220</code></a> Thanks <a href=\"https://github.com/matthewp\"><code>@​matthewp</code></a>! - Fixes a spurious 404 request for a dev toolbar sourcemap during <code>astro dev</code> caused by the browser mis-resolving a relative <code>sourceMappingURL</code> from the <code>/@id/</code> URL prefix</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><a href=\"https://redirect.github.com/withastro/astro/pull/16480\">#16480</a> <a href=\"https://github.com/withastro/astro/commit/1bcb43bf04f3fa8f4623897ae2a937250f35216a\"><code>1bcb43b</code></a> Thanks <a href=\"https://github.com/matthewp\"><code>@​matthewp</code></a>! It provides a new headless table primitive that enables powerful data table features while maintaining Kumo's design system consistency.\n\n## Changes\n- **New Block**: Added \\`TanstackTable\\` block component (\\`packages/kumo-docs-astro/src/components/blocks/TanstackTable.tsx\\`) with comprehensive table functionality including sorting, filtering, and pagination.\n- **Demo Updates**: \n  - Enhanced the existing \\`TableDemo\\` with improved examples\n  - Added new \\`TanstackTableDemo\\` showcasing advanced TanStack Table features\n- **Documentation**: Created new documentation page for the TanStack Table block\n- **Component Updates**: Refactored the core \\`table\\` component to work with the new TanStack integration\n- **Dependencies**: Added \\`@tanstack/react-table\\` to support the new table primitive\n\n## Testing\n- [ ] Manual testing completed with the new demo examples\n- [ ] Visual regression tests reviewed\n\n## Checklist\n- Reviews\n  - [ ] bonk has reviewed the change\n  - [ ] automated review not possible because: prototype feature requiring design review\n- Tests\n  - [ ] Tests included/updated\n  - [ ] Automated tests not possible - manual testing has been completed as follows: verified demos render correctly and table interactions work\n  - [ ] Additional testing not necessary because: prototype implementation",

      "body": "## Summary\n\n`Tabs` documents `TabsItem.render` as being for link-based tabs, but does not forward\nBase UI's `nativeButton` prop to `Tabs.Tab`. Since Base UI defaults `nativeButton` to\n`true`, every link-based tab logs a dev warning on mount, and there is no way to\nsilence it from application code.\n\n> A component that acts as a button expected a native `<button>` because the\n> `nativeButton` prop is true. Rendering a non-`<button>` removes native button\n> semantics, which can impact forms and accessibility. Use a real `<button>` in the\n> `render` prop, or set `nativeButton` to `false`.\n\nThe warning is dev-only and I could not find any user-visible breakage (see\n*Impact* below), but it fires once per tab bar per mount, so it shows up on every mount in apps\nthat follow the documented link-tab pattern.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n```tsx\nimport { Link } from \"@cloudflare/kumo/components/link\";\nimport { Tabs } from \"@cloudflare/kumo/components/tabs\";\n\n<Tabs\n  variant=\"underline\"\n  value={current}\n  tabs={[\n    { value: \"overview\", label: \"Overview\",\n      render: <Link href=\"/settings/overview\" className=\"no-underline\" /> },\n    { value: \"members\", label: \"Members\",\n      render: <Link href=\"/settings/members\" className=\"no-underline\" /> },\n  ]}\n/>\n```\n\n**Expected:** tabs render as real `<a href>` (so middle-click / copy-link-address /\ncontext menu work) with no console warning.\n\n**Actual:** tabs render correctly and navigate correctly, but the warning above is\nlogged on every mount. Measured with a Playwright probe (`page.on(\"console\")`): one\nwarning per page that has a link-based tab bar, zero on pages without one.\n\n## Root cause\n\n`Tabs` hand-picks the props it passes to Base UI's `Tabs.Tab`, and there is no rest\nspread on either `TabsProps` or `TabsItem` — so `nativeButton` cannot be reached from\napplication code at all:\n\n```js\n// dist/chunks/tabs-*.js (2.9.0, unminified)\nitems.map((tab) => jsx(TabsTab, {\n  \"data-kumo-component\": \"Tabs\",\n  \"data-kumo-part\": \"tab\",\n  value: tab.value,\n  render: tab.render,\n  onClick: (e) => { e.currentTarget.scrollIntoView({ /* … */ }); },\n  className: cn(/* … */, tab.className),\n  children: tab.label\n}, tab.value))\n```\n\nBase UI itself supports the prop — it is only the pass-through that is missing:\n\n```js\n// @base-ui/react 1.6.0 — tabs/tab/TabsTab\nconst { className, disabled = false, render, value, id: idProp,\n        nativeButton = true, style, ...elementProps } = componentProps;\n// …\nconst { getButtonProps, buttonRef } = useButton({\n  disabled, native: nativeButton, focusableWhenDisabled: true,\n});\n```\n\n`TabsItem` documents this use case, which is what sent us looking for the prop in the\nfirst place:\n\n```ts\n// dist/src/components/tabs/tabs.d.ts\n/**\n * Custom render function or element to replace the tab element (e.g. for link-based tabs).\n * …\n */\nrender?: TabsTab.Props[\"render\"];\n```\n\n**Affected versions:** reproduced on **2.8.0** and **2.9.0** (latest at time of\nwriting). The tab-construction code is identical in both, so upgrading does not help.\n\n## Impact\n\nLow, and I want to be accurate about it rather than overstate:\n\n`nativeButton` feeds Base UI's `useButton`, where it gates `tabIndex`, `aria-disabled`\nand the `disabled` attribute. But `TabsItem` has no `disabled` field and `Tabs` never\npasses `disabled` to `Tabs.Tab`, so those branches can't produce a user-visible\ndifference through Kumo's public API. In practice the cost is the console noise —\nwhich is still worth fixing, because the pattern that triggers it is the one the\ndocs recommend.\n\n## Proposed fix\n\nForward the prop from the item descriptor:\n\n```ts\nexport type TabsItem = {\n  value: string;\n  label: ReactNode;\n  className?: string;\n  render?: TabsTab.Props[\"render\"];\n  /** Set to false when `render` produces a non-<button> element (e.g. a link). */\n  nativeButton?: boolean;\n};\n```\n\n```js\njsx(TabsTab, {\n  // …\n  nativeButton: tab.nativeButton,\n})\n```\n\nI'd suggest an explicit prop rather than inferring it from `render` — `render` can\nlegitimately be a real `<button>`, so a heuristic would guess wrong in that case.\n\n## Workaround\n\nFor anyone hitting this before it's fixed: dropping to the Base UI primitives that\nKumo already re-exports works, at the cost of restating the tab styling.\n\n```tsx\nimport { Tabs as TabsPrimitive } from \"@cloudflare/kumo/primitives/tabs\";\n\n<TabsPrimitive.Tab value={item.value} nativeButton={false} render={<Link href={item.href} />}>\n  {item.label}\n</TabsPrimitive.Tab>\n```\n\n## Related\n\n#367 is the same Base UI warning surfacing through a different component\n(`DropdownMenu.Trigger`).\n\n## Environment\n\n- `@cloudflare/kumo` 2.8.0 and 2.9.0\n- `@base-ui/react` 1.6.0 (as bundled)\n- React 19.2, Chromium via Playwright 1.62\n\n",

      "body": "## Summary\n\n- Adds a new `Table.SortIcon` sub-component for use inside `Table.Head` to indicate sort direction.\n- The `direction` prop accepts `false | \"asc\" | \"desc\"` — matching TanStack Table's `column.getIsSorted()` return type exactly, so consumers can pass the value directly without any conversion.\n- Fixes `Table.ResizeHandle` to prevent click events from propagating to the column's sort handler after a drag.\n- Adds a TanStack Table integration demo to the docs showing sortable columns and draggable column resizing working together.\n\n## Usage\n\n```tsx\n// With TanStack Table — no conversion needed\nconst isSorted = header.column.getIsSorted(); // false | \"asc\" | \"desc\"\n<Table.SortIcon direction={isSorted} />\n\n// Standalone\n<Table.SortIcon direction=\"asc\" />\n```",

      "body": "Fixes internal Cloudflare ticket UI-8298.\r\n\r\n## Summary\r\n\r\n- Forwards the `toastManager` prop on `<Toasty>` through to the underlying\r\n  `<Toast.Provider>`, enabling toast dispatch from non-React-component code\r\n- Adds `createKumoToastManager` to the top-level `@cloudflare/kumo` barrel\r\n  (already available via the deep `@cloudflare/kumo/components/toast` path)\r\n- Adds tests covering the new prop, no-duplicate-root behavior with an\r\n  external manager, and shared-instance semantics with `useKumoToastManager`\r\n\r\n## Problem\r\n\r\n`<Toasty>` today only exposes toast dispatch via the `useKumoToastManager`\r\nhook, which is unusable outside React components. Consumers who need to\r\ndispatch toasts from module-load callbacks, timers, web workers, query-cache\r\nlisteners, or other non-component code have no canonical path.\r\n\r\n`@tanstack/react-query` cache event handlers run outside the\r\nReact tree. Wiring \"show a toast on every failed mutation\" through the\r\nexisting API requires a singleton handle pattern (set by a mount-time\r\ncomponent, read by the cache callback) — a workaround that exists in at\r\nleast one Cloudflare codebase today and that we'd like to retire.\r\n\r\nThe underlying `@base-ui/react/toast` already supports this via a\r\n`toastManager` prop on `<Toast.Provider>` — described in their docs as\r\n\"A global manager for toasts to use outside of a React component.\" Kumo's\r\n`<Toasty>` wraps `<Toast.Provider>` but does not forward this prop.\r\n\r\n## Solution\r\n\r\nThree changes:\r\n\r\n1. **`Toasty` accepts an optional `toastManager` prop.** When provided, it\r\n   is forwarded directly to the wrapped `<Toast.Provider>`. The prop type\r\n   is `ReturnType<typeof createKumoToastManager>`, which matches the\r\n   instance kumo's own `wrapManagerMethods()` produces (with dedupe-aware\r\n   `add`/`update`/`promise` behavior).\r\n\r\n2. **`createKumoToastManager` is exported from the top-level barrel.**\r\n   Previously only reachable via `@cloudflare/kumo/components/toast`. The\r\n   factory itself is unchanged.\r\n\r\n3. **Usage pattern.** Create the manager at module scope, pass it to\r\n   `<Toasty>`, and dispatch from anywhere:\r\n\r\n   ```tsx\r\n   // toast-manager.ts\r\n   import { createKumoToastManager } from \"@cloudflare/kumo\";\r\n   export const appToastManager = createKumoToastManager();\r\n\r\n   // app.tsx\r\n   <Toasty toastManager={appToastManager}>\r\n     <App />\r\n   </Toasty>\r\n\r\n   // from any non-component code\r\n   appToastManager.add({ title: \"Saved\" });\r\n   ```\r\n\r\n   `useKumoToastManager()` inside the tree returns the same underlying\r\n   manager instance, so in-tree and out-of-tree dispatch converge.\r\n\r\n## Breaking change?\r\n\r\nNo. The prop is optional; existing `<Toasty>` consumers and the existing\r\ntop-level barrel exports are unaffected. The `createKumoToastManager`\r\naddition to the top-level export is purely additive (it was already\r\nreachable via the deep path).\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n- Reviews\r\n  - [x] automated review not possible because: additive prop forwarding to a documented base-ui primitive; behavior matches the upstream contract\r\n- Tests\r\n  - [x] Tests included/updated",

\nRelease notes\n

Sourced from hono's releases.

\n
\n

v4.12.34

\n

Security fixes

\n

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

\n

memo() retains SSR output across requests, leading to cross-user data disclosure

\n

Affects: hono/jsx (server-side rendering). Fixes memo() reusing a retained render result across requests when props compare equal, where a component reading request-scoped values from ambient context — useContext(), useRequestContext(), or getContext() — could serve HTML rendered for another user's request, disclosing account data or request-scoped secrets such as CSRF tokens. GHSA-f23p-vx2j-j53r

\n

ReDoS in CORS middleware via Access-Control-Request-Headers

\n

Affects: hono/cors. Fixes a whitespace-tolerant regular expression with quadratic backtracking used to parse the Access-Control-Request-Headers preflight header when allowHeaders is not configured (the default), where a single preflight request carrying a long whitespace run could consume seconds of CPU and stall request processing. GHSA-8j4g-w8fx-2239

\n

Algorithmic complexity DoS in Language Middleware

\n

Affects: hono/language. Fixes quadratic string processing in language-tag normalization, where a crafted language tag with a large number of hyphen-separated subtags — supplied via a query parameter, cookie, or Accept-Language header — could cause excessive CPU consumption and block the event loop. GHSA-54fx-42gc-7vw4

\n

Proxy Helper does not remove response headers listed in the Connection header

\n

Affects: hono/proxy. Fixes proxy() forwarding response headers that the origin's Connection header designates as connection-scoped, where headers intended only for the immediate peer — per RFC 9110 Section 7.6.1 — could be exposed to clients, disclosing connection-scoped or internal metadata. GHSA-79qm-7rj5-m7r9

\n
\n

Users who use hono/jsx for server-side rendering, hono/cors, hono/language, or hono/proxy are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

        "message": "fix(code): Fix CodeHighlighted dark mode, layout, and SSR issues (#169)\n\n* fix(code): Fix CodeHighlighted dark mode, layout, and SSR issues\n\n- Fix dark mode: Make <pre> background transparent so container's\n  bg-kumo-base handles theming and border-radius is respected\n- Fix layout: Wrap Shiki output in overflow container to prevent\n  line highlight negative margins from being clipped\n- Fix width: Add w-full to container for proper full-width display\n- Fix SSR: Remove 'use client' directive from @cloudflare/kumo/code/server\n  entry point so server utilities work in RSC/SSR contexts\n\n* feat(code): Add CodeBlock component for SSR\n\nAdds a CodeBlock wrapper component to @cloudflare/kumo/code/server\nthat applies consistent styling to server-rendered Shiki HTML.\n\nUsage:\n  import { highlightCode, CodeBlock } from '@cloudflare/kumo/code/server';\n  const html = await highlightCode(code, 'tsx');\n  return <CodeBlock html={html} />;\n\n* fix(code): Add right padding to code element for overflow scrolling\n\nEnsures there's breathing room on the right side when code\noverflows horizontally and user scrolls.\n\n* fix(code): Fix JSX.Element type error in CodeBlock\n\nImport ReactNode from react and use it as return type instead of JSX.Element.",

        "message": "feat(code): Add Shiki-powered CodeHighlighted component (#163)\n\n* feat(code): add Shiki-powered CodeHighlighted component\n\n- Add ShikiProvider for lazy-loading Shiki at runtime\n- Add CodeHighlighted component with syntax highlighting\n- Add useShikiHighlighter hook for custom implementations\n- Add server utilities for SSR (highlightCode, createServerHighlighter)\n- Add cloudflare light/dark themes\n- Add @cloudflare/kumo/code entry point (tree-shakeable)\n- Add CSS for dual-theme support and line highlighting\n- Deprecate legacy Code and CodeBlock components\n- Add docs page and demos\n\n* fix(code): improve dark mode, copy button, and line numbers\n\n- Switch to github-light/vesper themes (remove custom cloudflare themes for now)\n- Fix dark mode by only applying background to container, not spans\n- Fix copy button placement for single-line snippets (inline instead of overlay)\n- Implement showLineNumbers prop with aligned line numbers column\n- Simplify docs overview section (less marketing-y)\n\n* style(code): remove line number border, use subtle opacity for line numbers\n\n* feat(code): add customizable highlight color via CSS variable\n\n- Add --kumo-code-highlight-bg CSS variable for line highlighting\n- Remove border between code and copy button on single-line snippets\n- Fix line highlighting in dark mode (exclude from transparent bg rule)\n- Add interactive demo for customizing highlight color in docs\n\n* feat(code): add i18n support for copy button labels\n\n- Add labels prop to ShikiProvider for app-wide localization\n- Add labels prop to CodeHighlighted for per-component overrides\n- Default labels: { copy: 'Copy', copied: 'Copied!' }\n- Update docs with i18n section and examples\n- Update all docs examples to use github-light/vesper themes\n\n* chore: add changeset\n\n* feat(code): hide copy button until hover\n\n* chore: remove cloudflare themes, fix lint rule false positives\n\n- Remove unused cloudflare/cloudflare-dark theme files\n- Remove ./code/themes export from package.json and vite.config\n- Fix no-tailwind-dark-variant lint rule to only match actual Tailwind classes\n  (e.g., dark:bg-blue-500) not object keys (e.g., { dark: \"vesper\" })\n\n* fix: hardcode themes to github-light and vesper (#164)\n\nRemove theme customization from the CodeHighlighted API:\n- Remove themes prop from ShikiProvider\n- Remove theme prop from CodeHighlighted\n- Hardcode github-light for light mode, vesper for dark mode\n- Update server utilities with hardcoded themes\n- Update documentation to reflect the change\n\n---------\n\nCo-authored-by: Charlie Gleason <hi@charliegleason.com>",

  "body": "## Problem\n\n`Sidebar.useIsMobile` reads `window.matchMedia` inside a `useState` initializer:\n\n```ts\nconst [isMobile, setIsMobile] = useState(() => {\n  if (typeof window === \"undefined\") return false;\n  return window.matchMedia(`(max-width: ${breakpoint - 1}px)`).matches;\n});\n```\n\nDuring SSR `window` is undefined, so `isMobile` is `false` (desktop) and the server renders the desktop `<aside>`. On a mobile viewport the client's first hydration render evaluates `matchMedia` → `true`, producing the **mobile overlay DOM** (a structurally different tree: backdrop + `<nav data-mobile>`). The SSR HTML and the client hydration render don't match → React logs a hard hydration mismatch error and re-renders client-side, discarding the SSR output.\n\nThis affects any SSR framework (e.g. Next.js) mounting `Sidebar` on a mobile viewport. Confirmed still present on `main` and in the latest published versions (2.9.2 / 2.10.0).\n\n## Fix\n\nSwitch `useIsMobile` to `useSyncExternalStore` with a desktop `getServerSnapshot`:\n\n- **Hydration is SSR-safe**: React renders with `getServerSnapshot` (`false`) during hydration, matching the SSR HTML, then switches to the real viewport once subscribed to `matchMedia`.\n- **No re-subscribe churn**: `subscribe`/`getSnapshot` are memoized on the query, so the `matchMedia` listener only re-binds when the `breakpoint` changes — same behavior as the previous `useEffect([breakpoint])`.\n\n```ts\nfunction useIsMobile(breakpoint: number = MOBILE_BREAKPOINT) {\n  const query = `(max-width: ${breakpoint - 1}px)`;\n\n  const subscribe = useCallback((callback: () => void) => {\n    const mql = window.matchMedia(query);\n    mql.addEventListener(\"change\", callback);\n    return () => mql.removeEventListener(\"change\", callback);\n  }, [query]);\n\n  const getSnapshot = useCallback(\n    () => window.matchMedia(query).matches,\n    [query],\n  );\n\n  const getServerSnapshot = useCallback(() => false, []);\n\n  return useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getServerSnapshot);\n}\n```\n\n## Tests\n\nAdded 4 unit tests in `sidebar.test.tsx` covering the SSR/hydration contract:\n\n- SSR renders the desktop `<aside>` regardless of the viewport (fails with the previous implementation).\n- `hydrateRoot` over the SSR output produces no hydration mismatch on a mobile viewport.\n- Client render on a mobile viewport yields the mobile overlay.\n- Client render on a desktop viewport yields the desktop `<aside>`.\n\n- Reviews\n  - [ ] bonk has reviewed the change\n  - [x] automated review not possible because: external contribution\n- Tests\n  - [x] Tests included/updated",

## Installation and compatibility

Official installation requires:

```bash
pnpm add @cloudflare/kumo @phosphor-icons/react
```

Kumo’s published peer ranges are:

- React: `^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0`
- React DOM: `^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0`
- `@phosphor-icons/react`: `^2.1.10`
- Optional: `zod` and `echarts` for relevant features

The project’s React 19.1.1 is compatible. Kumo documents Tailwind CSS **v4**; it does not publish Tailwind as a peer dependency. Its own package is developed against Tailwind `^4.1.17`, so this project’s Tailwind 4.3.3 is directionally aligned.

For this repository’s CSS location, the official Tailwind integration would require the equivalent of:

```css
@source "../../node_modules/@cloudflare/kumo/dist/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}";
@import "@cloudflare/kumo/styles/tailwind";
@import "tailwindcss";
```

Import order matters: Kumo styles must precede Tailwind. The `@source` directive is required because Tailwind v4 does not scan `node_modules` automatically. Kumo also provides a standalone CSS build for non-Tailwind projects.

## SSR and Cloudflare/TanStack Start concerns

Kumo targets React 18/19 and is built on Base UI, whose release history includes SSR and RSC fixes. Kumo’s build also emits `"use client"` for RSC compatibility. This is compatible with normal TanStack Start SSR, but Kumo is not a server-only component library.

Important caveats:

- There is no explicit Kumo/TanStack Start/Cloudflare Workers SSR compatibility matrix.
- Dialog, Popover, Tooltip, Select, and similar components use portals, normally into `document.body`. Base UI recommends an isolated application root; Kumo exposes `KumoPortalProvider`.
- The published `2.10.0` release had a known `Sidebar` hydration mismatch on SSR/mobile. The fix is merged in [PR #730](https://github.com/cloudflare/kumo/pull/730), with `2.10.1` still pending in [release PR #728](https://github.com/cloudflare/kumo/pull/728) when checked.
- Test Kumo components through TanStack Start SSR and the actual Workers runtime before adopting `Sidebar` or complex overlays broadly.

## Migration concerns and recommended scope

Kumo is not drop-in compatible with the current components:

- `Button` variants/sizes differ; current `accent`/`default`/`small` APIs need mapping.
- Kumo has no direct `Card` equivalent; `LayerCard` is a different compound component. Keep the existing card wrapper initially.
- Kumo `Input` encourages built-in labels, descriptions, and errors. Current sign-in fields use external labels; adapt accessibility markup to avoid Kumo’s development warnings.
- Replace nested `<Link><Button>` patterns with Kumo `LinkButton`, `LinkProvider`, or `render` composition.
- Kumo expects semantic tokens such as `bg-kumo-base`, `text-kumo-default`, and `ring-kumo-line`; the current dark custom palette and arbitrary `white/black` classes will require visual restyling.
- Kumo components are package-owned. Its CLI-installed blocks are source-owned and customizable, which may be preferable for page-level compositions.

**Recommendation:** make this a small M0 compatibility spike, not a wholesale rewrite. First validate package installation, Tailwind ordering, explicit Kumo color mode, portal isolation, TanStack Router link integration, and SSR hydration. Then migrate `Button`, `Input`, and `Badge` behind existing local wrappers while retaining `Card` and custom layout components. Use Kumo directly for new administration screens only after visual and SSR validation.

## Ambiguity

There is also an unrelated unscoped package, [`kumo-ui`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/kumo-ui), from [nevobit/kumo-ui](https://github.com/nevobit/kumo-ui). It is an old React 18 library (`0.2.1`, published in 2023) and is not Cloudflare Kumo. In this project, `@cloudflare/kumo` is the likely intended library.
